reference_basis.primary: astro-templates/owl/ — the Gilroy Roofers structure the operator pointed at (https://gilroy-roofing.vercel.app/). Scaffolded from the TEMPLATE, not from sites/gilroy-roofing/, because the template carries the service/area render fixes that Gilroy's src/ predates (see build-log 2026-07-29).
reference_basis.no_urls_scraped: No Firecrawl spend on reference URLs — the template IS the reference and it is local. The client's own site contributed brand/business context only, never layout.
reference_basis.client_site_role: brand + business context only. Their site is a stock GoHighLevel template; zero layout, component, or CSS structure taken from it.

palette._derivation: Operator supplied three values: CTA #c49029, primary background #ffffff, secondary background #0a0a0a. Every remaining token was re-derived and contrast-verified against those three rather than inherited from the owl defaults, per the instruction in astro-templates/owl/src/styles/tokens.css and the button-contrast section of the owl README.

contrast_audit.on-accent/accent (#0a0a0a on #c49029): 6.95 PASS AA (full 4.5 threshold, not just the 3:1 large-text allowance)
contrast_audit.accent-as-text on dark band (#c49029 on: 6.95 — comfortably clears the 3:1 the template needs on dark panels, and well above the owl default's 3.78
_notes: White on #c49029 measures 2.85:1 and FAILS even the large-text allowance — that is why --color-on-accent is near-black. Never hardcode `white` on an accent fill in this build.

--color-accent-ink is unchanged from the owl default #8a6420. That is a verified coincidence, not an inheritance: H4's gold sits at hue ~39deg, within a degree of the template default, so the same darkened ink is the correct derivation and it measures 5.35:1 on this client's white background.

--color-surface had to move off #ffffff. The owl default pairs a warm off-white page (#f7f5f0) with white cards; with the operator's white page, cards need the inverse — a faint warm neutral (#f6f5f2) so surfaces read as distinct without introducing a second brand colour.

typography._derivation: Template defaults retained. The client's site loads Inter, Roboto and Poppins — those are GoHighLevel scaffold defaults, not a brand typeface choice, so there is no client font worth honouring. Montserrat's geometric slab-adjacent weight also sits closer to the H4 logo's condensed grotesque letterforms than a serif display would.

spacing_radius_motion._note: Inherited from the owl template unchanged. Spacing scale, radii, and max-width are template concerns, never client-derived.

logo.decision: Use the client's EXISTING mark. Higgsfield generation was declined by the operator after the mark was found — it already appears on H4's physical yard signs and feather flags across a dozen job photos, and regenerating it would desync the site from their real-world signage.

variants.use: #c49029 on the #0a0a0a header/footer — ties the mark to the CTA colour
knockout over dark photo scrims where gold would compete with the accent CTA

logo.method: Deterministic alpha-preserving recolor via PIL. No AI generation, no credits spent, letterforms untouched.

imagery.policy: Client photography only. 40+ authentic Dayton-area job photos at 5712x4284 are available — there is no reason to touch stock here.
imagery.serve_from: public/img/ — downloaded and resized locally, never hotlinked. The originals sit on GoHighLevel's CDN (assets.cdn.filesafe.space), which vanishes the moment the client leaves that platform.
imagery.stock_excluded: 5 low-resolution images on the client's current site were identified as stock (clay-tile installer, window installer, generic house exteriors) and are excluded.
imagery.gap: Concrete, Flooring and Drywall have zero photo coverage. Per operator decision these render text-only; the owl service schema handles an unset about_photo by design rather than falling back to the hero.

anti_patterns: generic construction stock photo (handshake, diverse team in hardhats, hard-hat closeup)
Lucide icon rows (max 1 outline icon per section, semantic only)
"Trusted by 10,000+ customers" without a real, verified number
randomized section order — the owl fixed order is mandatory
Owl Roofing's own programme names ('We Give A Hoot', 'Protect Your Nest System', 'Get It Right Guarantee') — brand assets of the reference site, never to appear in a generated site
hardcoding `white` as a button label — fails at 2.85:1 on this client's accent
publishing a numeric review count or a licensed/insured/bonded claim — neither is first-party verified for this client
